created.description: How many policies the apply created.

deleted_names.description: The names it deleted, as many as fit. Absent when it deleted none.

truncated.description: `true` when more names were deleted than are listed. Absent when all of them are.

scope-version.description:
The scope's version after the write. The key keeps the management API's spelling; a
caller sends the value back as `if-scope-version`.

AppliedPolicyContext.description:
What one policy apply left behind: the value of `context.applied`.

The counts are exact. The list of deleted names is capped in size; `truncated` says when
it is shorter than `deleted`.

ApplyOutcome.description: Values of `apply_outcome`. A later release may add a value without a format change.

x-audit-descriptions.failed: The write was attempted and failed.
x-audit-descriptions.refused: Validation refused the policies before anything was written.

CedarApiAction.description: Values of `action_name`. A later release may add a value without a format change.

x-audit-descriptions.apply_cedar_policies: Create, update or delete the stored Cedar policies of a project or a warehouse.
x-audit-descriptions.get_cedar_policy: Read one stored Cedar policy of a project or a warehouse.
x-audit-descriptions.introspect_authorization: Introspect which actions another principal may perform on a resource.
x-audit-descriptions.list_cedar_policies: List the stored Cedar policies of a project or a warehouse.
x-audit-descriptions.list_cedar_policies_from_server_sources: List every Cedar policy the server-level sources provide.
x-audit-descriptions.reset_predefined_policies: Return a project or a warehouse to the shipped predefined-policy defaults.
x-audit-descriptions.toggle_predefined_policy:
Switch one predefined policy on or off for a project or a warehouse. Recorded once
per switch in a request.

providers_checked.description: IDs of all providers in the chain that were consulted (sorted).

ChainNoProviderCtx.description: Context of a `resolve_roles` record with outcome `no_provider_applicable`.

role_count.description: How many roles the user holds after every provider has answered.

roles.description: The roles the user holds, ordered by provider and source id.

ChainRolesResolvedCtx.description: Context of a `resolve_roles` record with outcome `roles_resolved`.

HandlerContext.description: The keys this product contributes to the record's `context` object. Another product's keys are described by its own schema.

applied.description: What a policy apply left behind, one count per operation.

break_glass.description: The break-glass reason the caller stated, which a policy may route on.

changes.description: The predefined-policy switches the request asked for.

scope_changes.description: The scope-policy writes and deletes the request asked for.

dry_run.description:
Whether the call only reports what it would do, changing nothing. Present on every
policy apply.

apply_outcome.description: How a policy apply ended when it did not apply. Absent when it applied.

apply_error.description: Why a policy apply did not apply, as the caller was told. Present with `apply_outcome`.

provider_id.description: The provider that ran the search, as it names itself in configuration.

filter.description: The LDAP filter the search ran with, after substitution.

count.description: How many entries the filter matched. Always more than one here.

provider_id.description: The provider that answered, as it names itself in configuration.

user_dn.description: The distinguished name the pattern was tested against.

pattern.description: The DN regex that did not match, verbatim from configuration.

LdapDnNoMatchCtx.description:
Context of an `ldap_resolve_roles` record with outcome `dn_no_match` (branching mode,
`else.mode = none`).

provider_id.description: The provider that answered, as it names itself in configuration.

attribute.description: The group-membership attribute that was read and found absent or empty.

provider_id.description: The provider that resolved the roles, as it names itself in configuration.

role_count.description: How many roles this provider resolved for the user.

provider_id.description: The provider that ran the search, as it names itself in configuration.

filter.description: The LDAP filter the search ran with, after substitution.

mode.description: Which resolution path was active when the lookup failed.

Operation.description: Values of `operation`. A later release may add a value without a format change.

x-audit-descriptions.admission_enforce_check: An external enforce endpoint was asked whether a caller may use this instance.
x-audit-descriptions.cached_role_provider: A cached role provider answered from its cache, not from its upstream.
x-audit-descriptions.ldap_resolve_roles: An LDAP provider resolved one user's roles.
x-audit-descriptions.resolve_roles: The provider chain resolved one user's roles, across every provider that handled them.

Outcome.description: Values of `outcome`. A later release may add a value without a format change.

x-audit-descriptions.ambiguous_user: An LDAP search matched more than one entry, so no principal could be resolved.
x-audit-descriptions.dn_no_match:
A branching provider's DN pattern did not match, and it is configured to assign no
roles in that case.
x-audit-descriptions.no_provider_applicable: No provider in the chain handled this user; they receive no provider-assigned roles.
x-audit-descriptions.no_roles: The user was found and carries no group membership, so the role list is empty.
x-audit-descriptions.role_withheld: An enforce check did not grant its admission role. The request itself may still stand.
x-audit-descriptions.roles_resolved: The provider chain resolved the user's roles.
x-audit-descriptions.stale_cache_fallback: One or more providers failed to refresh, and cached roles were served instead.
x-audit-descriptions.user_not_found: The user was not found, so the role list is empty.

id.description: Stable key of the policy, as the caller named it.

enabled.description: Whether the caller asked for the policy to be in force.

PolicyChange.description: One enablement change a request asked for.

changes.description: The changes the request asked for, as many as fit.

truncated.description: `true` when the request asked for more changes than are listed.

PolicyChangesContext.description:
The policy changes a request asked for: the value of `context.changes`.

The list is capped in size; `truncated` says when fewer changes are listed than were
asked for.

ResolveMode.description: Values of `mode`. A later release may add a value without a format change.

x-audit-descriptions.branch_else_attribute: Branching mode, `else.mode = attribute`: the DN did not match.
x-audit-descriptions.branch_else_none: Branching mode, `else.mode = none`: the DN did not match, so no roles are assigned.
x-audit-descriptions.branch_then: Branching mode, `then` branch: the DN matched the pattern.
x-audit-descriptions.branching: Branching mode, before the DN pattern was tested (for example, the user was not found).

ResolvedSource.description: Values of `sources`. A later release may add a value without a format change.

x-audit-descriptions.cache_hit: Roles were served from a cache that is still within its TTL.
x-audit-descriptions.fresh: Roles were fetched live from the upstream source (e.g. LDAP query).
x-audit-descriptions.in_request: Roles were extracted from in-request data (e.g. JWT token claims).
x-audit-descriptions.persisted:
Roles were read from a durable catalog-backed store with no TTL — e.g.
token roles persisted on a previous login, served for a user who is not
the live caller (DEFINER views).
x-audit-descriptions.stale_fallback: The upstream source failed but stale cached roles were served as fallback.

RoleProviderId.description:
Identifies the system of record that owns a role.

Must be non-empty and contain only lowercase ASCII letters (a-z), digits (0-9),
and hyphens (-). Must not contain the `~` separator or any other special characters.
Well-known values: `"lakekeeper"` (server-managed), `"oidc"`, `"ldap"`, etc.

role.description:
The role's id in this catalog. Absent when the role has no catalog row for this
answer: roles from a token or an admission gate, and roles resolved above projects.

provider_id.description: The provider that supplied the role.

source_id.description:
The role's id at the provider, for looking it up there. Absent when the operator
turned role source ids off.

RoleRecord.description:
A role a record names: `{"role": …, "provider_id": …, "source_id": …}`, the keys
Lakekeeper's own records name a role with.

writes.description: How many policies the request writes.

deletes.description:
How many it names for deletion. Zero for a `replace`, which can still remove every
policy the writes do not name.

replace.description: `true` when the request states the whole desired set, not a delta. Absent otherwise.

names.description: The names it asked for — writes first, then deletes — as many as fit.

truncated.description: `true` when more names were asked for than are listed. Absent when all of them are.

ScopePolicyChangesContext.description:
The writes and deletes a scope-policy apply was asked to make, recorded before it made
them: the value of `context.scope_changes`.

The counts are exact. The list of names is capped in size; `truncated` says when fewer
are listed than were asked for.

provider_ids.description: Sorted list of provider IDs whose fresh data could not be obtained.

gate.description: The admission gate that asked, as it names itself in configuration.

check.description: The check within that gate whose endpoint answered.

role.description:
The admission role this check would have granted, and did not. An admission role has
no catalog id.

cache_ttl_secs.description:
How long this answer may be replayed before the endpoint is asked
again, so a reader can bound the staleness of the requests that follow
without knowing the deployment's configuration.

WithheldContext.description: Context for the withheld-role audit record.
